questions.problem: Calculate the area of the parallelogram spanned by $u=⟨2,1,-1⟩$ and $v=⟨1,2,0⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}u\times v & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(1\cdot 0-2\cdot (-1))i-(2\cdot 0-1\cdot (-1))j+(2\cdot 2-1\cdot 1)k \\  & =2i-j+3k \\  & =⟨2,-1,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the corresponding parallelogram is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\,u\times v\,| \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{14}.\end{aligned}
$$

Calculate the area $A$ of the parallelogram spanned by $a=⟨1,0,0⟩$ and $b=⟨0,3,4⟩.$

$A=${{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}a\times b & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 4\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 0 \\ 3 & 4\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 4\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 3\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(0\cdot 4-0\cdot 3)i-(1\cdot 4-0\cdot 0)j+(1\cdot 3-0\cdot 0)k \\  & =0i-4j+3k \\  & =⟨0,-4,3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the corresponding parallelogram is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\,a\times b\,| \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{0+16+9} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Calculate the area of the triangle spanned by $r=⟨1,-2,3⟩$ and $t=⟨0,1,-2⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
Using the formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}r\times t & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-2 & 3 \\ 1 & -2\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =((-2)\cdot (-2)-3\cdot 1)i-(1\cdot (-2)-3\cdot 0)j+(1\cdot 1-(-2)\cdot 0)k \\  & =i+2j+k \\  & =⟨1,2,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the corresponding parallelogram is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\,r\times t\,| \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of the triangle is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}.
$$

questions.problem: Calculate the area of the $△\,ABC,$ if $A(5,0,5),$ $B(6,-1,4),$ $C(9,1,0).$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the vectors $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(6i-j+4k)-(5i+5k) \\  & =i-j-k \\  & =⟨1,-1,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(9i+j)-(5i+5k) \\  & =4i+j-5k \\  & =⟨4,1,-5⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the formula to compute the cross product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -1 & -1 \\ 4 & 1 & -5\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 4 & -5\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =((-1)\cdot (-5)-1\cdot (-1))i-(1\cdot (-5)-4\cdot (-1))j+(1\cdot 1-4\cdot (-1))k \\  & =6i+j+5k \\  & =⟨6,1,5⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC}| \\  & =\sqrt{{6}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{5}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{62}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $△\,ABC$ is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{\sqrt{62}}{2}.
$$

Now, using the formula to compute the cross product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{PQ}\times \overset{\to }{PR} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & 0 & 2 \\ -2 & 1 & -5\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ 1 & -5\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ -2 & -5\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(0\cdot (-5)-1\cdot 2)i-((-1)\cdot (-5)-(-2)\cdot 2)j+((-1)\cdot 1-(-2)\cdot 0)k \\  & =-2i-9j-k \\  & =⟨-2,-9,-1⟩.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{PQ}\times \overset{\to }{PR}| \\  & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(-9)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{86}.\end{aligned}

$$

First, we find the vectors $\overset{\to }{ST}$ and $\overset{\to }{SU}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{ST} & =t-s \\  & =(2i+3j+k)-(j+2k) \\  & =2i+2j-k \\  & =⟨2,2,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{SU} & =u-s \\  & =(4i+j+2k)-(j+2k) \\  & =4i+0j+0k \\  & =⟨4,0,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the formula to compute the cross product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{ST}\times \overset{\to }{SU} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 2 & -1 \\ 4 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 4 & 0\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(2\cdot 0-(-1)\cdot 0)i-(2\cdot 0-(-1)\cdot 4)j+(2\cdot 0-2\cdot 4)k \\  & =0i-4j-8k \\  & =⟨0,-4,-8⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overset{\to }{ST}$ and $\overset{\to }{SU}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{ST}\times \overset{\to }{SU}| \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-4)^{2}+(-8)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16+64} \\  & =\sqrt{80} \\  & =4\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $△\,STU$ is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{4\sqrt{5}}{2}=2\sqrt{5}.

questions.problem:
Calculate the length of the altitude $CH$ of the $△\,ABC$, if $A(-2,0,-1)$, $B(0,-2,-1)$, $C(-3,-2,0).$

$CH=${{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the length of the altitude $CH$ can be related to the area of $△\,ABC$ as follows:

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB
$$

So, to find $CH,$ we first find ${A}_{△}.$ To start, we find the vectors $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(-2j-k)-(-2i-k) \\  & =2i-2j \\  & =⟨2,-2,0⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(-3i-2j)-(-2i-k) \\  & =-i-2j+k \\  & =⟨-1,-2,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & -2 & 0 \\ -1 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-2 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}2 & -2 \\ -1 & -2\end{aligned}|k \\  & =((-2)\cdot 1-(-2)\cdot 0)i-(2\cdot 1-(-1)\cdot 0)j+(2\cdot (-2)-(-1)\cdot (-2))k \\  & =-2i-2j-6k \\  & =⟨-2,-2,-6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC}| \\  & =\sqrt{(-2)^{2}+(-2)^{2}+(-6)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{44} \\  & =2\sqrt{11}.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $△\,ABC$ is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{2\sqrt{11}}{2}=\sqrt{11}.
$$

Let's also compute $AB$ since it appears in the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =|\overset{\to }{AB}| \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, using the formula ${A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△} & =\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB \\ \sqrt{11} & =\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot 2\sqrt{2} \\ \sqrt{11} & =CH\cdot \sqrt{2} \\ CH & =\frac{\sqrt{11}}{\sqrt{2}} \\ CH & =\frac{\sqrt{22}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{SG}\times \overset{\to }{SM} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 0 & -2\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(1\cdot (-2)-2\cdot 0)i-((-3)\cdot (-2)-0\cdot 0)j+((-3)\cdot 2-0\cdot 1)k \\  & =-2i-6j-6k \\  & =⟨-2,-6,-6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overset{\to }{SG}$ and $\overset{\to }{SM}$ is

$$

$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $△\,GSM$ is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{2\sqrt{19}}{2}=\sqrt{19}.
$$

Let's also compute $SM$ since it appears in the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}SM & =|\overset{\to }{SM}| \\  & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, using the formula ${A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}GH\cdot SM,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△} & =\frac{1}{2}GH\cdot SM \\ \sqrt{19} & =\frac{1}{2}GH\cdot 2\sqrt{2} \\ \sqrt{19} & =GH\cdot \sqrt{2} \\ GH & =\frac{\sqrt{19}}{\sqrt{2}} \\ GH & =\frac{\sqrt{38}}{2}.\end{aligned}

Now, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{LM}\times \overset{\to }{LN} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & -1 & 3 \\ 2 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}|k \\  & =((-1)\cdot 1-0\cdot 3)i-(1\cdot 1-2\cdot 3)j+(1\cdot 0-2\cdot (-1))k \\  & =-i+5j+2k \\  & =⟨-1,5,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overset{\to }{LM}$ and $\overset{\to }{LN}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{LM}\times \overset{\to }{LN}| \\  & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{5}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{30}.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $△\,LMN$ is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{\sqrt{30}}{2}.
$$

Let's also compute $LN$ since it appears in the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}LN & =|\overset{\to }{LN}| \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, using the formula ${A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}MH\cdot LN,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△} & =\frac{1}{2}MH\cdot LN \\ \frac{\sqrt{30}}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}MH\cdot \sqrt{5} \\ \sqrt{30} & =MH\cdot \sqrt{5} \\ MH & =\frac{\sqrt{30}}{\sqrt{5}} \\ MH & =\sqrt{6}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Calculate the length of the altitude $HK$ of the $△\,GHI,$ if $G(1,1,1),$ $H(3,2,4),$ $I(2,4,2).$

$HK=${{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
Note that the length of the altitude $HK$ can be related to the area of $△\,GHI$ as follows:

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}HK\cdot GI
$$

So, to find $HK,$ we first find ${A}_{△}.$ To start, we find the vectors $\overset{\to }{GI}$ and $\overset{\to }{GH}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{GI} & =i-g \\  & =(2i+4j+2k)-(i+j+k) \\  & =i+3j+k \\  & =⟨1,3,1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{GH} & =h-g \\  & =(3i+2j+4k)-(i+j+k) \\  & =2i+j+3k \\  & =⟨2,1,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{GI}\times \overset{\to }{GH} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 3 & 1 \\ 2 & 1 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 1 \\ 1 & 3\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 2 & 3\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}1 & 3 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(3\cdot 3-1\cdot 1)i-(1\cdot 3-1\cdot 2)j+(1\cdot 1-3\cdot 2)k \\  & =8i-j-5k \\  & =⟨8,-1,-5⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overset{\to }{GI}$ and $\overset{\to }{GH}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{GI}\times \overset{\to }{GH}| \\  & =\sqrt{{8}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-5)^{2}} \\  & =3\sqrt{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $△\,GHI$ is

$$
{A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}A=\frac{3\sqrt{10}}{2}.
$$

Let's also compute $GI$ since it appears in the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}GI & =|\overset{\to }{GI}| \\  & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{11}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, using the formula ${A}_{△}=\frac{1}{2}HK\cdot GI,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3\sqrt{10}}{2} & =\frac{1}{2}HK\cdot \sqrt{11} \\ HK & =\frac{3\sqrt{10}}{\sqrt{11}} \\ HK & =\frac{3\sqrt{110}}{11}.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Area of the Triangle Spanned by Two Vectors
canonical_examples.problem: Calculate the area of the triangle spanned by $\mathbf{a}=\langle 4,0,-3 \rangle$ and $\mathbf{b}=\langle 5,-1,2 \rangle.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Using the formula, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}a\times b & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 4 & 0 & -3 \\ 5 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & -3 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}4 & -3 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 \\ 5 & -1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(0\cdot 2-(-3)\cdot (-1))i-(4\cdot 2-(-3)\cdot 5)j+(4\cdot (-1)-0\cdot 5)k \\  & =-3i-23j-4k \\  & =⟨-3,-23,-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the corresponding parallelogram is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\,a\times b\,| \\  & =\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+(-23)^{2}+(-4)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{554}.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of the triangle is

$$
A_{\triangle} = \dfrac{1}{2}A = \dfrac{\sqrt{554}}{2}.
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Calculate the area of the $\bigtriangleup\!ABC,$ if $A(1,0,-2),$ $B(-2,0,1),$ $C(1,1,-1).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we find the vectors $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(-2i+k)-(i-2k) \\  & =-3i+3k \\  & =⟨-3,0,3⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(i+j-k)-(i-2k) \\  & =j+k \\  & =⟨0,1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, using the formula to compute the cross product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -3 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}-3 & 3 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(0\cdot 1-3\cdot 1)i-(-3\cdot 1-3\cdot 0)j+(-3\cdot 1-0\cdot 0)k \\  & =-3i+3j-3k \\  & =⟨-3,3,-3⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC}| \\  & =\sqrt{(-3)^{2}+{3}^{2}+(-3)^{2}} \\  & =3\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $\bigtriangleup\!ABC$ is

$$
A_{\bigtriangleup} = \dfrac{1}{2}A = \dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}.
$$

canonical_examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Altitude of a Triangle Given Its Vertices
canonical_examples.problem: Calculate the length of the altitude $CH$ of the $\bigtriangleup\!ABC$ if $A(-1,1,0),$ $B(1,1,2),$ $C(1,-1,1).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Note that the length of the altitude (height) can be related to the area of the triangle as follows:

$$
A_{\bigtriangleup} = \dfrac{b \cdot h}{2},
$$

 
where $b$ is a base and $h$ is the corresponding altitude of the triangle.

For the $\bigtriangleup\!ABC,$ we have $h=CH,$ and $b=AB.$ So, we have

$$
A_{\bigtriangleup} = \dfrac{1}{2} CH \cdot AB.
$$

So, to find $CH,$ we first find $A_{\bigtriangleup}.$ To start, we find the vectors $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(i+j+2k)-(-i+j) \\  & =2i+2k \\  & =⟨2,0,2⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(i-j+k)-(-i+j) \\  & =2i-2j+k \\  & =⟨2,-2,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC} & =|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2 & 0 & 2 \\ 2 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|i-|\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ 2 & 1\end{aligned}|j+|\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}|k \\  & =(0\cdot 1-2\cdot (-2))i-(2\cdot 1-2\cdot 2)j+(2\cdot (-2)-0\cdot 2)k \\  & =4i+2j-4k \\  & =⟨4,2,-4⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the area of the parallelogram spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB}$ and $\overrightarrow{AC}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =|\overset{\to }{AB}\times \overset{\to }{AC}| \\  & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+{2}^{2}+(-4)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36} \\  & =6.\end{aligned}
$$

The area of the triangle is half of the area of the respective parallelogram. So, the area of $\bigtriangleup\!ABC$ is

$$
A_{\bigtriangleup} = \dfrac{1}{2}A = \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot 6 = 3.
$$

Let's also compute $AB$ since it appears in the formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}AB & =|\overset{\to }{AB}| \\  & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+{0}^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{8} \\  & =2\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Finally, using the formula $A_{\bigtriangleup} = \dfrac{1}{2} CH \cdot AB,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}_{△} & =\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot AB \\ 3 & =\frac{1}{2}CH\cdot 2\sqrt{2} \\ 3 & =CH\cdot \sqrt{2} \\ CH & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{2}} \\ CH & =\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
